english.title: Carry out relevant activity under unregistered foreign activity arrangement
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..)

(A)_[carried out a relevant activity, namely **(..SPECIFY ACTIVITY..),]_
(B)_[arranged for a relevant activity, namely **(..SPECIFY ACTIVITY..), to be carried out]_

in the United Kingdom pursuant to a foreign activity arrangement made by **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), and required to be registered under section 65(4) of the National Security Act 2023, when it was not so registered and you knew or, having regard to other matters known, ought reasonably to have known that you were acting pursuant to a foreign activity arrangement
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 67(3) and 80(1) of the National Security Act 2023.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
a foreign activity arrangement having been made by another person
that had not been registered under section 65 of the National Security Act 2023,
carried out a relevant activity OR arranged for a relevant activity to be carried out in the United Kingdom
knowing, or having regard to other matters known, you ought reasonably to have known
that you were acting pursuant to a foreign activity arrangement

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Sections 67(4) provides a defence to this offence available where the person has taken all steps reasonably practicable to determine whether the foreign activity arrangement that they are acting pursuant to was or was not registered, and having taken such steps, reasonably believed that it was registered.
(ii) If this this offence is committed, it is likely the offence under sections 65 will also apply (failure to register) see H101461.
(iii) Section 68 provides a second set of ‘enhanced tier’ registration requirements under the foreign influence registration scheme. Section 68 focusses on activities conducted by specified persons themselves, rather those that they are directing through an arrangement that would need to be registered under section 65. See H101464, H101464 and H101466 for offences under section 68.
(iv) Section 69 provides a requirement to register a foreign influence arrangement made with a foreign power. See H101467 for the associated offence.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or fine
Indictment : maximum 5 years imprisonment and / or fine

The maximum penalty on summary conviction depends on the general limit in a magistrates’ court and may be 6 or 12 months depending on the date of conviction, see section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.​​​​​​​
